Attention pieces and normalisation

Source: R/ops.R
zl-attention.Rd

zl_softmax() normalises each column (the first dimension) after multiplying by scale and adding mask, an additive f32 tensor whose first two dimensions are x's and whose third and fourth are 1 or x's, so one mask serves every head. zl_causal_mask() sets to -Inf every element of each matrix whose row index exceeds its column index, so that for scores of dims c(n_kv, n_q, ...) a query sees only keys at or before it.

Usage

zl_softmax(x, mask = NULL, scale = 1)

zl_causal_mask(x)

zl_rope(x, pos, n_dims, base = 10000, mode = c("interleaved", "half"))

zl_rms_norm(x, eps = 1e-05)

zl_layer_norm(x, eps = 1e-05)

Arguments

x, mask

Tensors.

scale

A number.

pos

An integer input of positions.

n_dims

The number of leading dimensions to rotate: even, at most head_dim.

base

The frequency base.

mode

"interleaved" or "half".

eps

Added to the mean square, a positive number.

Value

A tensor.

Details

zl_rope() applies rotary positions to x of dims c(head_dim, heads, n, ...) with integer positions pos of length n (an input declared with zl_int()). mode = "interleaved" rotates adjacent pairs ('ggml”s default and Toto's convention); mode = "half" rotates the first half against the second (TimesFM, Chronos-2, most Hugging Face checkpoints). n_dims below head_dim rotates the leading n_dims only.

zl_rms_norm() divides each column by its root mean square; zl_layer_norm() subtracts the column mean first.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
g <- zl_graph(
  function(x) zl_softmax(zl_causal_mask(x$s)),
  p,
  inputs = list(s = c(3, 3))
)
zl_forward(g, list(s = matrix(0, 3, 3)))$output
#>      [,1] [,2]      [,3]
#> [1,]    1  0.5 0.3333333
#> [2,]    0  0.5 0.3333333
#> [3,]    0  0.0 0.3333333
